prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on what kind of trip you want. For convenience, reliability and on‑site amenities (especially for short stays or show nights) pick a hotel on/near the 76 “Strip” or Branson Landing. For privacy, space, a kitchen, lakeside views or a true cabin experience pick an Airbnb/cabin near Table Rock Lake or Branson West. Below are quick recommendations by trip type plus booking tips.

Which to choose — quick pros/cons
- Hotel — Pros: predictable service, daily housekeeping, on‑site restaurants/concierge/parking, easy check‑in/out, often closer to shows and nightlife. Good for short stays, couples wanting convenience, business travel, or if you don’t want to manage a rental. Cons: less space, no kitchen, can be pricier per person for families/groups.
- Airbnb/cabin/VRBO — Pros: more space, kitchens, lower per‑person cost for groups, private cabins and docks on Table Rock Lake, better for families/groups or longer stays. Cons: variable quality, fewer on‑site services, sometimes minimum nights and extra cleaning/clean‑up responsibilities.

Best neighborhoods by purpose
- Branson Strip (76 Country Boulevard): best for shows, restaurants, attractions — stay here if you want walkable nightlife and short drives to theaters.
- Branson Landing / downtown: good mix of shops, restaurants, lakefront walks and easy access to shows.
- Table Rock Lake / Hollister / Ridgedale area: best for lakefront cabins, boating, fishing and quieter stays.
- Branson West / near Silver Dollar City: best if visiting Silver Dollar City or wanting Ozark outdoors and cabin rentals.

Top specific picks (by style)
- Luxury lakeside resorts
  - Chateau on the Lake Resort, Spa & Convention Center — upscale, lake views, spa and on‑site dining (good for romantic or pampering stays).
  - Big Cedar Lodge (nearby, in Ridgedale) — high‑end rustic resort with cabins, lots of outdoor activities (excellent for outdoorsy couples/families).
- Comfortable resort/condo options
  - Welk Resort Branson — condo units and resort amenities, good for families/groups who want kitchens and pools.
  - Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing — convenient lakeside hotel next to shops/dining at Branson Landing (good mid/upper range hotel).
- Good dependable hotels (convenient for shows)
  - Radisson Hotel Branson (well‑known brand; convenient locations vary) and other national chains along the Strip — good value and predictable service.
- Best for cabins/Airbnb stays
  - Table Rock Lake cabins (search for “dock + cabin + Table Rock Lake” or “lakefront cabin Branson”) — ideal for boating/fishing, lakefront views and privacy.
  - Branson West/Silver Dollar City area cabins — good if your trip centers on Silver Dollar City.
  - Downtown/Branson Landing condos (Airbnb) — mix of hotel convenience with kitchen/living space.

Booking tips and what to look for
- If you pick Airbnb/VRBO: look for Superhosts, recent 5‑star reviews, whole‑place listing, clear cancellation policy, free/clear parking, good Wi‑Fi if you need it, and check cleanliness and stairs/ADA details. Confirm proximity to the Strip or the lake depending on your plan.
- If you pick hotels: check show schedules and distance to the theaters you’ll attend — traffic can get heavy on show nights. Look for free parking, breakfast options, and shuttle service if available.
- Timing: peak seasons (late spring–summer and holiday show seasons like Thanksgiving–Christmas) book early — aim for 6–12+ weeks ahead in high season, earlier for popular cabins.
- Families/groups: a cabin or condo with a kitchen will usually save money and make evenings easier.
- If you want nightlife and walking access to multiple theaters, prefer a hotel on the Strip or Branson Landing.

If you tell me your travel dates, how many people, budget, and whether you want lake access or show/nightlife focus, I’ll give 3–5 specific up‑to‑date listings (hotels and Airbnb examples) that match your needs.
